question: What intimate familial relationship does the speaker claim toward the goddess and her mother?
premises: The speaker addresses the great goddess as beloved.
He refers to her mother in relation to her.
He declares himself to be her husband.
inference: The speaker claims the role of husband to the goddess in this familial context.
uncertainties: The compound tva-umātu is textually compressed and its exact syntactic relation is uncertain.
plain_english: O great goddess, O beloved, I am your husband, in relation to you and your mother.
